hints: A common subsequence preserves character order in both strings but can skip characters.
Let dp[i][j] be the longest common subsequence length for the two prefixes.
Matching final characters extend the diagonal; otherwise discard one final character and take the better result.
analogy: For two text strips, keep a shared character only if it appears in order in both.
example: For 'ABC' and 'AC', the longest common subsequence is 'AC' of length 2.
algorithm: Fill an (n+1) by (m+1) table: if characters match, dp[i][j]=dp[i-1][j-1]+1; else max(dp[i-1][j],dp[i][j-1]). Store choices or backtrack to output the sequence if required.
correctness: Any common subsequence either uses matching final characters together or omits at least one of them; the recurrence considers those exhaustive possibilities.
complexity: O(nm) time and O(nm) space for reconstruction.
